title: Mrs. Bectors Food Specialities Ltd - 543253 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Mrs. Bectors FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore (+9.1%) but EBITDA grew only 2.5% to INR257.7 crore, with margin at 12.6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 8.9% YoY to INR485.86 crore, with Biscuits up 8.4% and Bakery up 8.5%, and Bakery EBITDA margin at 12.7% (+25 bps). FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,043.6 crore (+9.1%), EBITDA INR257.7 crore (+2.5%, margin 12.6%) and PAT INR140.9 crore (6.9% margin). Management flagged a new cost shock from the West Asia conflict (about 3% cost impact on packaging, palm oil, crude-linked items, labour and logistics), which it says is covered by price increases and Project IMPACT savings. Export incentive (DFIA) remains on hold, and exports stayed in low-single-digit growth in Q4.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.4% YoY and FY26 grew 6.7%; management targets low-to-mid-teens growth in FY27. About 65% of biscuit sales come from INR5 and INR10 packs.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 8.5% with Navratri shifting into March. FY26 grew 14%. Management guides mid-teens Bakery growth in FY27, with English Oven at high-teens and QSR at low-teens. Premiumisation is about 55-56% for English Oven.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Low-single-digit growth in Q4 and single-digit for FY26, hit by US tariffs (peak 50%) and the West Asia conflict. FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens growth; the Bahrain and Kuwait GCC markets are affected.

segments.name: Frozen / value-added bakery
segments.commentary: Sells raw dough, baked bread and ready sandwiches, partly sourced from third parties. Growing month-on-month on quick commerce in Delhi NCR. NaturBaked targets about INR10 crore ARR.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Biscuits growth guided at low-to-mid-teens; Bakery at mid-teens; exports at low-to-mid-teens.
Price increases and cost efficiency expected to offset about 3% West Asia-related cost inflation, keeping value addition in line in H1 FY27.
EBITDA margin expected to improve QoQ in Q1 and again in Q2 FY27; management says the objective is 'as close as possible to 14%' but did not commit to it.
Management expects to sustain YoY EBITDA margin unless crude moves sharply above USD100; logistics cost impact may show in Q2.
Outlet count to rise by 40,000 (from 310,000-320,000 billed outlets) in FY27. Target 2030: 40-45% weighted availability in North India (currently about 35%) and 900,000-1 million total outlets.
capex_capacity: Kolkata bakery plant commissioned in January 2026, giving entry into East India.
Mumbai bakery plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and is in ramp-up; English Oven Mumbai is the largest opportunity, where management sees room to scale about 3x.
Khopoli bun line commissioned and running; bread line nearing completion, with products to roll out by quarter-end. Utilisation not disclosed.
Indore biscuit plant is now operational, and distribution will expand into Central and part of Western India. Rajpura remains the main North plant.
A Bangalore facility is under consideration. Each plant is planned to produce burger buns and value-added products, including sourdough and frozen dough.
demand_pricing: Competitor INR4.5 pack pricing post GST 2.0 hurt Q3 and Q4 biscuit volumes; management called it an aberration and said one large player is still transitioning to the right coin pricing.
Management expects a tailwind from GST-driven grammage increases and lower MRPs to fade as inflation drives price sensitivity.
Wheat crop was good; the Bakery QSR wheat cost is locked for the year, and biscuit wheat exposure is limited to gluten. Hedging is done selectively for wheat flour, sugar, milk powder and edible oil.
Quick commerce is a growing channel: English Oven holds a high-single-digit share on Q-com in Kolkata; a Valentine's Blinkit collaboration reached over 300,000 households.
US tariffs were cut from their 50% peak, and new US retailer projects have started onboarding. Export incentive (DFIA) restart is still pending with the government.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the current RM and wheat inflation, and can margins be protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil, crude-linked items and packaging are the main drivers. Total impact is about 3% including labour and logistics, mostly covered by pricing and cost efficiency, with logistics impact still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bakery growth slow to 9% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Navratri moved into March (from April last year), which hit bread demand in North India. Management called it seasonal and said English Oven is still growing at high-teens.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin hold YoY and can it reach 14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin improvement in Q1 and Q2, and says margin should be maintained YoY unless crude spikes sharply. It stated the objective is to get as close as possible to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and status of the export incentive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew in single digits in FY26 and low single digits in Q4; FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens. The DFIA incentive restart is still pending, and cost and price actions partly offset its loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of INR5 and INR10 packs and is there commodity hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: INR5 and INR10 packs make up about 65% of biscuit sales, in line with the industry. Hedging is selective, and the hedge levels are not disclosed.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and crude-driven inflation in packaging, palm oil, fuel and logistics, with the logistics impact expected in Q2 FY27.
Competitive pricing risk: a large player still transitioning from INR4.5 price points, which could affect volumes or pricing.
Export incentive (DFIA) hold remains unresolved; GCC exports (Bahrain, Kuwait) are impacted.
Khopoli bun line utilisation was not disclosed, and the new Mumbai plant is still ramping up.
Minimum wage hikes in UP and Karnataka add to cost pressure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Biscuits and Bakery growth recovery and FY27 targets, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly qualified its outlook for the uncertain cost environment and declined to quantify utilisation and hedge levels.
key_quotes: We are very confident of touching on the biscuit segment somewhere between low to mid-teens kind of growth in this financial year.
So we should be able to cover up to not impact on our margins negatively on EBITDA margin side and also on the gross margin side.

growth.why: FY27 guided at low-to-mid-teens Biscuits, mid-teens Bakery and low-to-mid-teens exports, backed by newly commissioned Kolkata, Mumbai, Khopoli and Indore capacity, price increases, and 40,000 new outlets, though no specific order or contract figures were given and utilisation was not disclosed.
